newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: YACHTING-MORNING GLORY WINS HOBART, BREAKS RECORD.
newsitem.headline: YACHTING-MORNING GLORY WINS HOBART, BREAKS RECORD.

text.p: German maxi Morning Glory won the 52nd Sydney-to-Hobart yacht race on Sunday, breaking the 21-year race record by around 30 minutes.

The 24.5-metre (80-foot) maxi crossed the finish line in Hobart, Tasmania, at 3.06 a.m. (local) breaking the race record of two days 14 hours 36 minutes and 56 seconds set by U.S. maxi Kialoa in 1975.

Morning Glory needed to finish by 3.36 a.m.(local, 1636GMT) on Sunday to break the record. In the past two years the lead yacht has been well within the race record charging down the east coast of Tasmania, only to be becalmed and robbed of the record.
Morning Glory will collect A$300,000 (US$237,000) the richest prizemoney for a record-breaking line honours win in a single ocean race.

The win and record by Morning Glory is a remarkable comeback for the German maxi, which broke its mast only days before the start, forcing a frantic mission to fly a replacement mast from New Zealand in time for the start on Thursday.
Hong Kong pocket maxi Exile was expected to finish second in the 630 nautical mile race within the next few hours.
